<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a straightforward binary package that downloads pre-built binaries from the project's own GitHub releases. The sources download from `https://github.com/roman-16/proton-cli/releases/download/v${pkgver}/` - the project's own upstream, which is the expected source for a binary package.

There is no `pkgver()` function, no top-level command substitutions, and no code that executes when the PKGBUILD is sourced. The architecture-specific sources use standard variable interpolation for the version number. Both source tarballs have SHA256 checksums provided (not SKIP), though even if they were SKIP, that would not be grounds to fail this narrow gate since extraction does not execute the content.

The `package()` function is standard packaging code (installing the binary, symlinks, and shell completions), but it is not executed during `--nobuild --noprepare`, so it is out of scope for this gate.

This is consistent with normal AUR binary package practices with no indicators of malicious behavior.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>

Standard binary AUR package from project's own GitHub releases.</summary>
</security_assessment>
